questions.question: Who can declare an area to be a development area under the Telangana Urban Areas (Development) Act?
questions.key_facts: The Government, by notification (section 13(1)).

questions.question: What must a Master Plan for a development area define?
questions.key_facts: The zones of the development area, how land in each zone is to be used, and the stages of development; a framework for zonal development plans (section 6(2)).

questions.question: If the development authority does not decide on my application for development permission, when is permission deemed to be granted?
questions.key_facts: If neither granted nor refused within ninety days of the application or of the further information, permission is deemed granted (section 14(5)).

questions.question: What documents must accompany an application for development permission to the Authority?
questions.key_facts: The prescribed fee, a copy of the title deed attested by a Gazetted Officer, and an urban land ceiling clearance certificate or an affidavit that holdings are within the ceiling (section 14(2)).

questions.question: Is the application fee refunded if development permission is refused?
questions.key_facts: No; the applicant is not entitled to a refund (section 14(8)).

questions.question: What is the penalty for developing land without the Authority's permission?
questions.key_facts: Imprisonment up to three years, or a fine up to 20% of the land value fixed by the Registration Department, or both; plus up to 1% of that value per day for a continuing offence (section 41(1)).

questions.question: What is the maximum rate of development charges per square metre?
questions.key_facts: Rs 300 per sq m for development of land and Rs 125 per sq m of floor area for buildings (section 28(2) proviso).

questions.question: How much time does an owner get to remove an unauthorised development after a demolition order?
questions.key_facts: Not less than five and not more than fifteen days from delivery of the order (section 42(1)).

questions.question: How can I appeal against an assessment of development charges, and within what time?
questions.key_facts: Appeal to the Tribunal within two months of the order being communicated, with a fee not exceeding Rs 250 (section 31).

questions.question: Can I buy a plot in an unapproved layout now and still regularise it under LRS 2020?
questions.key_facts: No; only plots with a registered sale deed executed before 26-08-2020 qualify (Q11).

questions.question: How much must be paid when applying for regularisation of an individual plot under LRS 2020?
questions.key_facts: Rs 1,000 for an individual plot (Rs 10,000 for a layout) with the application; the balance by 31-01-2021, in instalments (Q15).

questions.question: Will a plot that falls on a proposed Master Plan road be regularised under LRS?
questions.key_facts: No; plots affected by a Master Plan road will not be regularised (Q10).

questions.question: I built a house on a plot in an unapproved layout. Can the building be regularised under LRS?
questions.key_facts: The plot can be regularised; there is at present no provision to regularise unauthorised buildings (Q16).

questions.question: What is a Bhudhaar and what determines a permanent Bhudhaar?
questions.key_facts: A number automatically assigned to every land parcel; the permanent one considers the parcel's location, its shape from corner-point coordinates, and ownership in the Record of Rights (section 9(1)).

questions.question: After a sale of agricultural land is registered, who updates the Record of Rights?
questions.key_facts: The Tahsildar, immediately after registration, moves the land from the transferor's to the transferee's account (section 5(5)).

questions.question: Where do I appeal against a Tahsildar's order amending the Record of Rights, and within how many days?
questions.key_facts: To the Revenue Divisional Officer within sixty days of the order being communicated (section 15(1)).

questions.question: Can I file a second appeal after the Revenue Divisional Officer decides my Record of Rights appeal?
questions.key_facts: Yes, to the District Collector within thirty days; the Collector's decision is final (section 15(4)).

questions.question: Are entries in the Record of Rights presumed to be correct?
questions.key_facts: Yes, presumed true and correct until the contrary is proved or the entry is amended under the Act (section 11).

questions.question: Can agricultural land be used for a non-agricultural purpose without permission?
questions.key_facts: No; prior permission of the competent authority is required, applied for with the conversion tax (section 3).

questions.question: What happens if the conversion tax I paid for converting agricultural land is less than required?
questions.key_facts: The authority sends a notice of the deficit within 30 days, payable within 15 days; with no notice in 30 days the amount is deemed sufficient (section 3(3)-(5)).
